S1 (overwrite replaced_by drops in-force content) — hosting.extended.yaml, hosting_ext_overdue_renewal.overwrite[0] (lines 1626-1636) and hosting_ext_early_renewal.overwrite[0] (lines 2511-2521), both retiring base hosting_renewal clause:
  superseded_clause: "A renewal is billed at the regular rate of the tier and term length that the new term will have (renewal_rate_12mo, renewal_rate_24mo or renewal_rate_36mo times the months, or monthly_rate_no_commitment for a 1-month term, with no setup fee), less the account tier's hosting_discount_pct, rounded half up to the cent."
  replaced_by (in-force part for out-of-scope renewals): "... every other renewal, which is an auto-renew charge, a renewal that applies a scheduled downgrade request, or a renewal paid at checkout while the term end date is later than today for a plan with a scheduled term change request, is billed at the regular rate of the tier and term length that the new term will have, less the account tier's hosting_discount_pct, rounded half up to the cent."
  Dropped in-force content: the parenthetical "(renewal_rate_12mo, renewal_rate_24mo or renewal_rate_36mo times the months, or monthly_rate_no_commitment for a 1-month term, with no setup fee)". Once the base clause is published as no longer in force, auto-renew charges, downgrade-applying renewals and checkout renewals with a scheduled term change have no in-force statement that the per-month regular rate is multiplied by the months of the term, that a 1-month term renews at monthly_rate_no_commitment, or that no setup fee is billed. (The extended rules' own "regular price for the new term length: ... times the months ... with no setup fee" sentences are scoped to the overdue / early renewal amount only.) Same defect in both policies; the two replaced_by texts should restate the parenthetical for the "every other renewal" class.

S2 (rule vs tool docstring/body) — hosting_ext_auto_renew_refund.rule (line 2341-2342), also base hosting_auto_renew_refund: "The refund goes to refund_destination_default, or to account credit when the customer elects it or the charge was paid from credit."
  vs task_tools.py refund_hosting_auto_renewal_84b3efde: no destination parameter; body always books refund_destination="original_payment_method" (and the return contract fixes "refund_destination (original_payment_method)"); docstring: "returns the stated refund amount to the payment method that paid the auto-renew charge". A customer election of account credit cannot be booked, and a refund of a line paid from account credit is recorded as original_payment_method rather than account_credit (so the hosting_refund -> account:account_credit_refund trigger never fires). Either the tool needs a destination parameter (original_payment_method | account_credit, account_credit forced for a credit-paid line) or the rule must state the destination the tool books.
